open_findings.claim: AC-8 puts the branch requirement in a test (`git branch --show-current` is `stats`), which a unit test suite cannot observe reliably, so the criterion has no result a test can check.
open_findings.failure_scenario: The suite runs in CI on a detached HEAD or another branch name, or the test is skipped. Either the test fails for a correct build or no test checks the branch at all.

open_findings.claim: The request says a malformed stored value is reported, with no exemption. AC-6 narrows this by never checking done tasks' due dates and priorities, and done tasks' tags unless --tag is given.
open_findings.failure_scenario: A done task 4 has priority `urgent`. The request item 5 reads as exit 2 naming task 4. The spec requires exit 0 for plain `stats`, so a reader of the request would see a mismatch. The choice is recorded only as a risk and was not confirmed.

open_findings.claim: No test checks that a done task's bad due date or priority is ignored under --tag, although AC-6 says they are not checked at all except without --tag being irrelevant.
open_findings.failure_scenario: An implementation that validates all tasks' due and priority whenever --tag is given would exit 2 on a file with a done task having due 'bad' under `stats --tag x`; every test still passes because the done-task due/priority case is only run in plain `stats`.

open_findings.claim: AC-6 'first offending task by id' is never tested with two offenders in the same field, so an implementation reporting the last (or any) offender passes.
open_findings.failure_scenario: File with open tasks 3 and 5 both having bad due dates: code that reports task 5 (e.g. iterating in reverse) passes all tests, since every test has only one offender per field.

open_findings.claim: No test checks that under --tag a done task's bad due date or priority is still ignored (AC-6 says only done tags are checked with --tag).
open_findings.failure_scenario: A change makes cmd_stats validate due/priority of all tasks when --tag is given; `stats --tag x` on a file with a done task with due 'bad' would exit 2, and every test still passes.
